conventions.commits: Conventional Commits (CONTRIBUTING.md), committed with git commit -S --signoff for GPG signing and DCO. Language commits follow the form 'feat(core): add <Lang> language support with tree-sitter-<lang> handler (#NNNN)', as in the Swift commit dbc2971 (#1742).
conventions.testing: Inline #[cfg(test)] mod tests at the bottom of each languages/<lang>.rs (queries_compile, set_language_smoke, element/inheritance/defuse happy and edge paths); registration tests in lang.rs and languages/mod.rs; tool-level tests in crates/aptu-coder/tests/*.rs using common::call_tool_raw and tempfile::NamedTempFile::with_suffix_in. Test names use the test_<lang>_<behaviour> or queries_compile style.
conventions.linting: cargo clippy -- -D warnings (CI uses --locked --profile ci), cargo fmt --check, cargo deny check advisories licenses bans (deny.toml; bans multiple-versions is warn). Workspace clippy deny lints: undocumented_unsafe_blocks, unwrap_used, expect_used (test code exempt). Warn lints: must_use_candidate, redundant_clone, needless_pass_by_value, large_enum_variant. REUSE compliance requires an SPDX header on each new file.
conventions.error_handling: Handlers return Option or Vec<String> and never panic; get_node_text() bounds-checks byte ranges and returns Option. Query compile failures surface as ParserError::QueryError (parser.rs build_compiled_queries). get_language_info returns Option<LanguageInfo>, and None means unsupported.

patterns: Each language is one handler file under languages/ exporting ELEMENT_QUERY, CALL_QUERY, REFERENCE_QUERY, IMPORT_QUERY, DEFUSE_QUERY as &str constants, plus optional extract_* handler fns (java.rs, swift.rs).
Registry: languages/mod.rs get_language_info() returns a LanguageInfo literal per language with Some(...) or None for every optional field; get_ts_language() maps the name to a tree_sitter::Language.
Extension routing: lang.rs EXTENSION_MAP tuple list plus a supported_languages() slice; language_for_extension() is a case-insensitive linear search.

Element capture contract (parser_elements.rs ~275-300): @function with @func_name or @method_name for functions and methods; @class with @class_name or @type_name for types. When no name capture is present, the name falls back to child_by_field_name("name").
Inheritance: handler signature fn(&Node, &str) -> Vec<String> returning labelled strings such as 'extends X' and 'implements Y' (java.rs, swift.rs 'extends'/'conforms').

Def-use: write captures use the prefix write., write.local, write.assign, write.property; read captures use read.usage; writeread.* for updates. Read captures are dropped when a write capture exists at the same start byte.
Lazy per-language query compilation (#1786, commit 4d714d9) caches compiled queries per language name, so new languages pay no startup cost.
Shared enclosing_function_name() already recognises method_declaration and function_definition, so PHP needs no change there.

approaches.name: A. Java-parity handler on grammar-verified node kinds (recommended)
approaches.description: Add languages/php.rs with ELEMENT_QUERY (function_definition, method_declaration, class/interface/trait/enum declarations), CALL_QUERY (function_call_expression, member_call_expression, nullsafe_member_call_expression, scoped_call_expression), REFERENCE_QUERY (named_type name), IMPORT_QUERY (namespace_use_declaration), DEFUSE_QUERY (variable_name writes and reads), and extract_inheritance that iterates children of kind base_clause and class_interface_clause. Use LANGUAGE_PHP. No receiver or function-name handlers. Wire into workspace and core Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, mod.rs (mod decl, get_language_info arm, get_ts_language arm, test table), lang.rs (EXTENSION_MAP, supported_languages, test), README.md, and one integration test file.
pros: Matches the issue's acceptance criteria one for one
Same shape as Java and Swift, so reviewers already know the pattern
Every node kind and field used is confirmed in node-types.json and define-grammar.js
Keeps the handler surface small and avoids the receiver-handler removal from #1807
cons: Query constants can only be proven by compiling them in a unit test; they are not yet run against the grammar
The defuse symbol convention ($x vs x) needs a decision before tests are written
Unfielded base_clause and class_interface_clause need a kind-based walk, which is slightly more code than Java's field access

approaches.name: B. Seed queries from upstream queries/tags.scm
approaches.description: Start from the upstream queries/tags.scm (interface, trait, class, function, method, class_interface_clause, function_call_expression, scoped_call_expression, member_call_expression) and rename its captures to aptu's contract (@function with @func_name/@method_name, @class with @class_name, @call). Add the enum_declaration pattern by hand because tags.scm does not include enums or imports. Otherwise identical wiring to A.
pros: Starts from node-kind and field combinations the upstream maintainers already use
Reduces guesswork on reference patterns such as qualified_name and variable_name in function calls
cons: tags.scm uses @definition.* and @reference.* captures that the aptu parser does not read, so each capture needs renaming
tags.scm has no enum_declaration or namespace_use_declaration patterns
Upstream reference patterns include object_creation_expression, which is outside the issue's call scope

approaches.name: C. Full Java parity including receiver handlers and trait use
approaches.description: As A, plus extract_function_name, find_method_for_receiver and find_receiver_type handlers modelled on java.rs, and use_declaration handling for trait use inside class bodies.
pros: Closest feature parity with Java and C#
Enables receiver-type metadata if a future consumer appears
cons: Explicitly out of scope in #1864 (receiver handlers have had no consumer since #1807)
Violates the acceptance criteria and the 'do not implement features not specified' rule in AGENTS.md
Adds about 3 extra handler functions and tests with no current caller

recommendation: Approach A, with B used only as a cross-check of node names. A meets every acceptance criterion in #1864, follows the Java and Swift templates the issue names, and uses only grammar-confirmed node kinds. C is excluded by the issue's scope fence. Before writing tests, decide the DEFUSE symbol convention. The draft below captures the whole variable_name node, so the symbol passed in must include the leading $ (for example '$z'). Capturing the inner name node instead would make the symbol 'z'. Either choice must be stated in the unit test. DEFUSE_QUERY is required, not optional: parser.rs compiles it only when the Option is Some, and parser_elements.rs returns an empty def-use result when it is None, so omitting it would silently disable def-use for PHP.

inheritance_walk_citation:
Grammar source: common/define-grammar.js in tree-sitter/tree-sitter-php (php/grammar.js is a 3-line wrapper that calls defineGrammar('php')). Rules as read:
(1) class_declaration: $ => prec.right(seq(optional(field('attributes', $.attribute_list)), repeat($._modifier), keyword('class'), field('name', reserved('classes', $.name)), optional($.base_clause), optional($.class_interface_clause), field('body', $.declaration_list))). Only 'name', 'body' and 'attributes' are fields; base_clause and class_interface_clause are unfielded children.
(2) base_clause: $ => seq(keyword('extends'), commaSep1($._name)). For a class, this is the 'extends' list. For an interface it is also the list of parent interfaces.
(3) class_interface_clause: $ => seq(keyword('implements'), commaSep1($._name)).
(4) enum_declaration includes optional($.class_interface_clause) with no base_clause, so enums can only have implements.
(5) The node-types.json entry for class_declaration lists children including 'base_clause' and 'class_interface_clause' and fields {attributes, body, name}. The entries for base_clause and class_interface_clause list children ['name', 'qualified_name', 'relative_name'].
Walk: name = node.child_by_field_name("name"); for i in 0..node.child_count(): if child(i).kind() == "base_clause", for each named_child of kind name, qualified_name or relative_name push "extends {text}"; if child(i).kind() == "class_interface_clause", push "implements {text}" for each such named child. Do not use child_by_field_name for these two clauses; it returns None.
